The current system can result in sticker shock for homeowners who do not fully understand how property taxes are calculated and adjusted in Florida. The governor's proposal aims to provide relief across the state, though the specific details of the modifications being considered by lawmakers have not been fully disclosed.

The legislative changes reflect ongoing negotiations between state lawmakers, the governor's office, and local government representatives who must balance tax relief for residents with the need to fund essential services. Lawmakers are expected to continue deliberations Tuesday before bringing the modified proposal to the floor for votes in both chambers. The outcome of this special session will determine whether Florida residents see property tax cuts and how those cuts will be structured across different counties and municipalities.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie woman faces attempted murder, arson charges after house fire on Southeast Airoso Boulevard
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie woman is facing charges including attempted murder and arson after allegedly setting fire to a bedroom door while a 62-year-old woman was inside the room Sunday night.

According to the Port St. Lucie Police Department, officers responded to reports of a domestic disturbance and active house fire at around 9:05 p.m. in the 1500 block of Southeast Airoso Boulevard. When they arrived, they found flames inside the residence and immediately worked to evacuate everyone safely.

The investigation revealed that the victim first noticed smoke coming from underneath her bedroom door and discovered Michelle Picard, 26, standing nearby when she opened it. When the victim attempted to retrieve a fire extinguisher, Picard allegedly physically attacked her and tried to prevent her from putting out the fire. Police say Picard made threatening statements and attempted to push the victim toward the flames.

The victim managed to escape to a bathroom, lock the door, and call 911. During the emergency call, Picard could be heard banging on the bathroom door in the background. Officers found Picard outside the residence and detained her. She resisted arrest, causing injuries to one officer's leg and requiring another officer to use a Taser.

Jose Tsu Zamora, 64, faces multiple felony charges following the incident at First United Methodist Church on Southwest Prima Vista Boulevard on Sunday morning. The attempted kidnapping unfolded around 10:49 a.m. in the church parking lot, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

Zamora, who previously had a romantic relationship with the victim, approached the 74-year-old woman despite an active injunction prohibiting any contact with her. Police say Zamora, while armed with a handgun, grabbed the victim by her arms and attempted to force her into his vehicle against her will.

Several witnesses saw the incident and immediately intervened. Two Good Samaritans confronted Zamora and ordered him to release the victim. During the confrontation, Zamora displayed his firearm before retreating to his vehicle and fleeing the scene, police said. Church surveillance footage captured portions of the encounter and corroborated witness statements, showing Zamora pursuing the victim.

Rivera lost clothes, furniture and irreplaceable personal belongings, including photos of her late son who passed away three years ago. The damage left Rivera displaced. She is uninsured and is now staying at her nephew's home while she rebuilds.

Rivera, who is also disabled, was recovering from neck fusion surgery the same week she lost her home. A memorial outside the damaged home is one of the few things Rivera has left that cannot be replaced.

cards.headline: Historic Fort Pierce landmark reopens as downtown dining destination

cards.body:
The Boston House, a downtown Fort Pierce staple for more than a century, has officially reopened as a new dining experience. Built in 1909 along South Indian River Drive, the home is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and has served a variety of roles over the decades.

Originally built by an engineer for Henry Flagler's Florida East Coast Railway, who later became St. Lucie County's third sheriff, the Boston House remains closely tied to the region's early development. Co-owner Georgette Angelos said the goal is to make guests feel at home while honoring the building's legacy.

During renovations, the owners intentionally preserved historic details, including low original ceilings and Florida-themed law books that nod to the home's past. General manager Scott Laird said the revival of the property reflects broader changes happening in the city.

cards.body:
Ninety-one firefighters and their families gathered at the Maltz Jupiter Theatre on Monday as Jupiter officially launched Jupiter Fire Rescue, and its newest members took their oath of service. For Fire Chief Darrel Donatto, the ceremony marked the culmination of more than two years of work building a department from the ground up.

Among the newest members is Lieutenant Christian Lainhart, a sixth-generation Jupiter resident. After years serving with Martin County Fire Rescue, he saw the chance to serve at home. His wife, Jessica Lainhart, also grew up in Jupiter and watched her husband become one of the first firefighters in the town's history.

cards.headline: Florida lawmakers debate sweeping property tax changes in Tallahassee special session
cards.teaser: Florida lawmakers returned to the Capitol Monday for a three-day special session on property taxes, weighing changes that could eventually eliminate property taxes on primary residences.
cards.body:
Florida lawmakers returned to the Capitol on Monday for a high-stakes, three-day special session on property taxes. Gov. Ron DeSantis is urging the Republican-controlled Legislature to approve a proposed constitutional amendment that would expand the homestead exemption and create a pathway toward eventually eliminating property taxes on primary residences.

The proposal would create a new $150,000 homestead exemption in 2027 and raise it to $250,000 in 2028 for homeowners who establish permanent Florida residency by the end of 2026. The exemption would then increase with inflation. Lawmakers would also be directed to establish a process allowing counties, municipalities and school districts to expand the exemption further, potentially eliminating homestead property taxes entirely.

The plan would also lower the annual assessment cap for non-homestead properties, including businesses and second homes, from 10% to 5%. It would restrict how counties and cities may spend remaining property tax revenue.

cards.body:

Current state law doesn't consider summer school a regularly scheduled education program, which is required to trigger enforcement. Barnes hinted that if the cameras stay in place, summer enforcement might eventually happen.

Since the cameras were installed, they've issued more than 21,000 tickets, with October being the peak month at 5,100 tickets. Barnes says the data proves the cameras work and speed reductions are considerable.

Wellington residents have had strong opinions on both sides. Some see them as essential for child safety, while others question the village's true motives.

The U.S. Soccer Federation began using the site in 2020 and has since hosted dozens of national youth team training camps. This year, seven Major League Soccer teams used it as a training site. Word spread internationally after Real Madrid used the facility last year.

Parts of South Florida are facing the possibility of severe thunderstorms and flash flooding on Tuesday. Weather forecasters are monitoring conditions that could produce dangerous weather across the region.

Central Florida is also expected to see strong storms developing Tuesday afternoon, with scattered storms forecast after 3 p.m. Coverage is expected to become more widespread into the afternoon and evening, particularly along Atlantic coastal counties. Warm temperatures and increasing humidity are creating favorable conditions for thunderstorm development across the region.

hero.headline: 5 injured in multi-vehicle crash on I-95 near Stuart, one vehicle catches fire
hero.body:
Five people were hospitalized Monday night after a multi-vehicle crash on Interstate 95 that sparked a vehicle fire, according to Martin County Fire Rescue.

The collision occurred just before 10 p.m. on I-95 northbound near Exit 101 and Halpatiokee Regional Park. Martin County Fire Rescue responded to the scene, where they found one of the vehicles on fire. Crews quickly extinguished the flames.

Two people suffered traumatic injuries and were transported to the hospital, while three others sustained minor injuries and were also taken for medical treatment. All northbound lanes of I-95 were closed while law enforcement investigated the crash. As of Tuesday morning, all lanes have reopened.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie woman faces attempted murder, arson charges after house fire on Southeast Airoso Boulevard
hero.body:
A Port St. Lucie woman is facing charges including attempted murder and arson after allegedly setting fire to a bedroom door while a 62-year-old woman was inside the room Sunday night.

According to the Port St. Lucie Police Department, officers responded to reports of a domestic disturbance and active house fire at around 9:05 p.m. in the 1500 block of Southeast Airoso Boulevard. When they arrived, they found flames inside the residence and immediately worked to evacuate everyone safely.

The investigation revealed that the victim first noticed smoke coming from underneath her bedroom door and discovered Michelle Picard, 26, standing nearby when she opened it. When the victim attempted to retrieve a fire extinguisher, Picard allegedly physically attacked her and tried to prevent her from putting out the fire. Police say Picard made threatening statements and attempted to push the victim toward the flames.

The victim managed to escape to a bathroom, lock the door, and call 911. During the emergency call, Picard could be heard banging on the bathroom door in the background. Officers found Picard outside the residence and detained her. She resisted arrest, causing injuries to one officer's leg and requiring another officer to use a Taser.

cards.headline: Man arrested after attempted armed kidnapping at Port St. Lucie church
cards.teaser: A North Miami man was arrested Sunday evening after allegedly attempting to kidnap a 74-year-old woman at gunpoint in a Port St. Lucie church parking lot.
cards.body:
Jose Tsu Zamora, 64, faces multiple felony charges following the incident at First United Methodist Church on Southwest Prima Vista Boulevard on Sunday morning. The attempted kidnapping unfolded around 10:49 a.m. in the church parking lot, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

Zamora, who previously had a romantic relationship with the victim, approached the 74-year-old woman despite an active injunction prohibiting any contact with her. Police say Zamora, while armed with a handgun, grabbed the victim by her arms and attempted to force her into his vehicle against her will.

Several witnesses saw the incident and immediately intervened. Two Good Samaritans confronted Zamora and ordered him to release the victim. During the confrontation, Zamora displayed his firearm before retreating to his vehicle and fleeing the scene, police said. Church surveillance footage captured portions of the encounter and corroborated witness statements, showing Zamora pursuing the victim.

cards.headline: Former St. Lucie County school bus driver faces additional charge as second victim comes forward
cards.teaser: A former St. Lucie County school bus driver is facing an additional charge after a second victim came forward in an ongoing investigation into allegations of inappropriate conduct with children.
cards.body:
Edwin Garcia, 72, of Port St. Lucie, was arrested on a new battery charge May 28 when a second victim came forward with additional information for investigators. This comes after his initial arrest March 6 on two counts of lewd and lascivious molestation of a victim under 12 years of age.

The investigation began March 4 when a school resource deputy received a report that Garcia had allegedly asked a 9-year-old student to lift her dress while riding the school bus. During the preliminary investigation, deputies developed additional information suggesting Garcia may have made inappropriate comments to the child and possibly pinched her over her clothing in the pelvic area, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office.

The Sheriff's Office continues to investigate the allegations and is encouraging anyone who may have been a victim or has additional information to come forward. Anyone with information related to this case can contact Detective Corporal Hunter Limb at (772) 462-7300.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce woman displaced after lightning strike destroys her home, loses irreplaceable belongings
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce woman is displaced and calling for help after a lightning strike tore through her home last month, leaving her with broken windows, heavy damage, and almost nothing left.
cards.body:
Rosa Rivera returned home from getting a haircut at church last month when a utility worker stopped her outside. A utility worker told her he thought her house was on fire. St. Lucie County District Firefighters rushed to put out the flames. Rivera was told a lightning strike caused the fire.

Rivera lost clothes, furniture and irreplaceable personal belongings including photos of her late son. The damage left Rivera displaced. She is uninsured and is now staying at her nephew's home while she rebuilds. Rivera, who is also disabled, was recovering from neck fusion surgery the same week she lost her home.

A memorial outside the damaged home is one of the few things Rivera has left that cannot be replaced. Despite everything, Rivera said she remains hopeful.

cards.headline: Historic Boston House in Fort Pierce reopens as downtown dining destination
cards.teaser: The Boston House, a downtown Fort Pierce staple for more than a century, has officially reopened as a new dining experience.
cards.body:
Built in 1909 along South Indian River Drive, the home is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and has served a variety of roles over the decades. Now, its newest owners are working to preserve its past while reimagining its purpose. Co-owner Georgette Angelos said the goal behind its historic doors is simple: make guests feel at home while honoring the building's legacy.

Originally built by an engineer for Henry Flagler's Florida East Coast Railway, who later became St. Lucie County's third sheriff, the Boston House remains closely tied to the region's early development. During renovations, the owners intentionally preserved historic details, including low original ceilings and Florida-themed law books that nod to the home's past.

General manager Scott Laird said the revival of the property reflects broader changes in downtown Fort Pierce.
